newsitem.title: USA: Calif tax measure threatens local finance-official.
newsitem.headline: Calif tax measure threatens local finance-official.

text.p: Los Angeles County Supervisor Zev Yaroslavsky said on Monday that a controversial California tax measure was a threat to local government finances.
At a press conference in Los Angeles, Yaroslavsky denounced Proposition 218 as a "direct assault" on Los Angeles County residents.
Municipal finance analysts have warned that Proposition 218 would seriously constrain local governments' ability to impose fees, assessments and taxes.
The measure would apply to all cities, counties, special districts, redevelopment agencies and school districts in California.
While the measure would reduce the amount of fees and taxes that individuals and businesses pay, it would decrease spending for local public services, analysts said.

"This measure not only endangers our long-term fiscal solvency," Yaroslavsky said. "More importantly, it poses a mortal danger to some of our most basic services such as sheriff's patrols and fire suppression, not to mention park and library operations, as well as others."

The proposition, which will appear on the November 5 state ballot, could virtually wipe out property-related assessments and force public programs to rely on increasingly scarce general fund dollars, the supervisor warned.
"Prop. 218 undermines the most fundamental concept of home-rule and political self-determination," Yaroslavsky said. "It's just bad policy."
Last week, Fitch Investors Service Inc warned that the proposition, if approved by California voters in November, would have a negative effect on municipal credit quality.
